News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / Philippine Elections Philippine Elections LIST: Comelec cancels registration of 50 party-list groups By: Chelsy Claire Perez - @inquirerdotnet INQUIRER.net / 04:46 PM October 22, 2026 Share: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has canceled the registration of 50 party-list groups, including Bayan Muna, for failing to meet participation or electoral performance requirements.
Under Resolution 11281, the poll body revoked the registration of party-list groups, organizations and coalitions that either failed to participate in the two preceding elections or failed to meet the requirements for securing seats in the party-list system.
Ten party-list groups, organizations and coalitions failed to participate in the two preceding elections:

The remaining 40 party-list groups failed to secure at least 2% of the votes cast for the party-list system and win a seat in the second round of allocation in either of the two preceding elections.
The cancellations were based on Republic Act 7941, or the Party-List System Act, and Comelec Resolution 11204, as amended.
Under Section 6(8) of the law, the Comelec may cancel a party-list group’s registration after due notice and hearing if it fails to participate in the two preceding elections or obtain the required votes. The poll body may act on its own initiative or upon a verified complaint from an interested party.
The cancellations enforce the statutory requirements for party-list registration and eligibility.
The Comelec also said party-list groups whose registrations remain valid must still file a manifestation of intent to participate in the 2028 elections.
Separate petitions may still be filed to seek the cancellation or disqualification of these groups or their nominees. /das
